newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end up on technicals, arbitrage.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end up on technicals, arbitrage.

text.p: Mexican stocks shrugged off a slump on Wall Street to end higher Thursday, buoyed by a technical rebound and bargain hunting.
"We had a technical rebound where the market validated support at 3,700 points, and ended shy of resistance at 3,750 points," Hector Jimenez, a technical analyst atthe Inverlat brokerage.
The leading IPC share index ended up 25.12 points, or 0.68 percent, at 3,741.30.
"The market is defending itself, we may even see a rally when the Dow settles down," Jimenez added.
Traders meanwhile put gains on share prices down to speculative buying spurred by a combination of factors.
"There was a bit of everything, short-covering, bargain-hunting and arbitrage, too, in the wake of a slide by the peso," a floor trader said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts had closed three centavos weaker at 7.9610 per dollar.
Among individual issues, Telmex gained 32 centavos (4 cents) to 15.66 pesos ($1.97). Telmex ADRs gained 5/8 to 39-1/4 on Wall Street.
Telmex accounted for 32 percent of the moderate 53.96 million shares traded in Mexico.
Traders said volume was low due to caution that was still present in the market.
On the broad market, 108 stocks changed hands, of which 50 ended up while 35 were down.

Retail group Salinas y Rocha L shares topped the prominent gainers' list, up 3 centavos (less than one cent) to 46 centavos (6 cents). Dealers said the stock gained on favourable department store sales figures published this week, while some said rumours of a "change of hands" in a controlling stake were responsable.
Debt stricken congolmerate Grupo Sidek was near the head of the prominent sliders' list, down 2 centavos (less than one cent) to 37 centavos (5 cents).
